title: Can two different solids show a rectangle and a triangle?
description: The video looks for two different solids that each show a rectangular profile from one viewpoint and a triangular profile from another. It tries a tent shaped prism and a square pyramid. Keeko's doubt is that only the tent shaped prism works.
teaching_notes: One idea: a solid is not fixed by its profiles, and a square is a rectangle with equal sides. Watch for students who think only one solid can fit the condition.

source: Give two different solids that each show a rectangular profi
video_script.why: The child has met profiles in the book and now finds that more than one solid can fit the same pair of profiles.
video_script.substitution: Try a solid from each side, look at it from two viewpoints, and name the outlines.
video_script.anchor: a tent shaped prism and a pyramid with a square base, each seen from two viewpoints
video_script.wrong_answer: only the tent shaped prism works
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks only the tent shaped prism works. The square pyramid shows a triangle from the side and a square from above, and a square is a rectangle with equal sides, so it works too.
video_script.payoff_line: A triangular prism and a square pyramid both work, and there are more

final_answer.value: A triangular prism and a square pyramid, among others
final_answer.spoken: a triangular prism and a square pyramid, among others

hold_back: Answer: A triangular prism and a square pyramid, among others
never_show: the tent shaped prism marked as the only solid
maths_rules: triangular prism: from the front a triangle, from the side a rectangle
square pyramid: from the side a triangle, from above a square
a square is a rectangle with equal sides
both solids pass the test, and other solids may pass too
video_script.design: Each solid stands on the stage in turn; the view point moves to two places and the outline of each view is drawn beside it with its name.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the profiles of solids.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Give two different solids. Each must show a rectangular profile from one viewpoint, and a triangular profile from another.

beats.on_screen: Given: one profile is a rectangle; the other profile is a triangle.
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, one profile is a rectangle, and the other profile is a triangle.

beats.on_screen: To find: two different solids with these two profiles

marks.find: the words two different solids are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find two different solids that fit.

beats.on_screen: Triangular prism: from the front a triangle, from the side a rectangle. It works.

narration: <bookmark mark='prism'/>Step one, try a tent shaped triangular prism.
<bookmark mark='front'/>From the front, the outline of the prism is a triangle.
<bookmark mark='side'/>From the side, the outline is a rectangle, so this solid fits both profiles.

beats.on_screen: Square pyramid: from the side a triangle, from above a square. A square is a rectangle with equal sides. It works.

marks.side: the view from the side is outlined as a triangle
marks.above: the view from above is outlined as a square and labelled a rectangle with equal sides

narration: <bookmark mark='pyramid'/>Step two, try a pyramid with a square base.
<bookmark mark='side'/>From the side, the outline of the pyramid is a triangle.
<bookmark mark='above'/>From above you see a square. A square is a rectangle with equal sides, so this solid works too.

beats.on_screen: Both solids fit. Other solids may fit too.

marks.both: both solids are ticked side by side

narration: <bookmark mark='both'/>Step three, compare the two. Both solids give a rectangle and a triangle, so a pair of profiles does not fix one solid.

beats.on_screen: Answer: A triangular prism and a square pyramid, among others
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>A triangular prism and a square pyramid both work, and there are more.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the two solids
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows only the tent shaped prism, struck through; the square from above the pyramid is shown beside a rectangle with equal sides

marks.doubt: the bubble appears beside the two solids
marks.square: the square from above the pyramid is shown beside a rectangle that is stretched until its sides are equal
marks.fix: the bubble is struck through and the pyramid is ticked

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks only the tent shaped prism works, because a square is not a rectangle.
<bookmark mark='square'/>A square has four right angles, and its opposite sides are equal. That is a rectangle, with all four sides equal.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The square pyramid works too. More than one solid can fit.
